title: The Crumb Inside the Atom
set_language: ONE persistent Cambridge 1897 cathode-ray lab set: long glass tube, glowing beam, magnet, charged plates, swap-in electrodes. Later: 1904 plum-pudding model. Say 'same 1897 Cambridge tube set'. Never 'same DNA'. Never name Thomson in Flow prompts.
continuity_lock: No Explorer this part. Readable finished face for the Cambridge physicist (moustache, round glasses) — describe, do not name. Picture change every 4–6 s.
explorer_lock: NONE this part. Film-wide Explorer budget: 1 used (Part 02); remaining for Parts 04/05 only.
forbidden: HARD REJECT: Orbit; photoreal; Ken Burns; gore; lava drip; DNA helix; Explorer; naming Thomson/Mendeleev/Dalton in the prompt; garbled dials; SEE labels.
motion_lock: Real Veo motion every plate. No freeze-pad.
quality_note: Veo 3.1 Quality for tube beam / glow plates. Fast otherwise.
board_split_2026_09_27: Split prior 8-plate board into 19 plates ≤~6 s for picture-change rule.

plates.vo_land: Cambridge, eighteen ninety-seven. J.J. Thomson is studying a strange glow.
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Cambridge 1897 lab. Bearded physicist with moustache and round glasses stands at a long glass cathode-ray tube on a wooden bench. Continuous approach to the tube. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. No readable fake text.
plates.prompt_try2: Same 1897 Cambridge lab. Wider: long glass tube on the bench, physicist silhouette at the far end. Continuous soft camera push. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit.

plates.vo_land: Cambridge, eighteen ninety-seven. J.J. Thomson is studying a strange glow.
plates.prompt: Same 1897 Cambridge tube set. Soft clean glow inside the long glass tube — careful emissive light, no lava drip. Continuous gentle beam shimmer. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit.
plates.prompt_try2: Same tube set. ECU of the glowing path inside the glass — clean Quality glow, no molten bead. Continuous shimmer. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Pump the air out of a glass tube, run electricity through it, and a beam shoots from one end to the other.
plates.prompt: Same 1897 Cambridge tube set. A clean glowing beam shoots from one end of the evacuated glass tube to the other. Continuous shoot. Quality glow. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. No lava.
plates.prompt_try2: Same tube. Side view: beam races left to right through the tube. Continuous race. Quality. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Scientists called them cathode rays. But what were they made of? Light, or stuff?
plates.prompt: Same 1897 Cambridge tube set. Beam holds while the camera drifts — question mood, curious wonder. Continuous drift. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. No text signs.
plates.prompt_try2: Same tube. Physicist leans in toward the glowing path, puzzled. Continuous lean. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Thomson brings a magnet close. The beam bends.
plates.prompt: Same tube set. A horseshoe magnet approaches the glass — the glowing beam bends. Continuous bend. Quality glow. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. No lava.
plates.prompt_try2: Same tube. MCU: magnet tip near the tube; beam curves away. Continuous curve. Quality. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: He tries two charged metal plates. It bends again.
plates.prompt: Same tube set. Two charged metal plates flank the tube — the glowing beam bends again. Continuous second bend. Quality glow. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit.
plates.prompt_try2: Same tube. Plates slide into place; beam deflects. Continuous deflect. Quality. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Light doesn't do that. Tiny charged particles do.
plates.prompt: Same tube set. Tiny charged crumbs stream along the bent path — not a straight light ray. Continuous crumb stream. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. No DNA helix.
plates.prompt_try2: Same set. Split visual: straight light ray fails; crumb path bends. Continuous contrast. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Then he measures how far they bend, and works out how heavy they must be.
plates.prompt: Same 1897 Cambridge tube set. Physicist measures the bend with a simple scale beside the tube. Continuous measure. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. No garbled dial numbers as hero.
plates.prompt_try2: Same set. Hands mark the deflection distance on a wooden rule. Continuous mark. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: The answer is astonishing: far lighter than a hydrogen atom, the lightest thing anyone knew.
plates.prompt: Cartoon compare: a tiny glowing crumb next to a much larger hydrogen-atom ball. Continuous size contrast. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. No garbled H tile.
plates.prompt_try2: Same idea. Tiny crumb floats past a big soft hydrogen sphere. Continuous float-past. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: We now know each one is about two thousand times lighter.
plates.prompt: Same crumb vs hydrogen visual. The crumb shrinks further — astonishing lightness. Continuous shrink. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. No text numbers in plate.
plates.prompt_try2: MCU crumb pulsing tiny beside the hydrogen ball. Continuous pulse. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: But here is the strange part. It doesn't matter which metal he uses.
plates.prompt: Same 1897 Cambridge tube set. Different metal electrode tips swap into the tube ends. Continuous swap. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit.
plates.prompt_try2: Same set. Hands exchange brass, then darker metal tips on the tube. Continuous exchange. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: The same particles come out every time.
plates.prompt: Same tube set. After each electrode swap, the same tiny glowing particles stream out. Continuous same-stream. Quality glow. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. No lava.
plates.prompt_try2: Same tube. Identical crumb streams from swapped tips. Continuous repeat. Quality. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: So the uncuttable thing can be cut. Every atom carries these tiny negative particles.
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. A soft cartoon atom cracks open; tiny negative crumbs spill inside. Continuous crack. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. No gore. No DNA helix.
plates.prompt_try2: Same atom crack, wider: shell splits, crumbs glow gently inside. Continuous split. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Thomson called them corpuscles. Today we call them electrons.
plates.prompt: Same cracked-atom set. Tiny negative crumbs orbit gently inside the soft shell. Continuous orbit. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit robot. No text labels in plate.
plates.prompt_try2: MCU of three tiny crumbs drifting inside the atom shell. Continuous drift. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: But atoms have no overall charge, so something positive must balance them out.
plates.prompt: Same atom model. Soft positive glow fills the sphere while negative crumbs sit inside — balanced. Continuous fill. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. No lava drip.
plates.prompt_try2: Atom sphere warms with soft positive light around the crumbs. Continuous warm-up. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: A few years later, in nineteen-oh-four, Thomson made his guess: a soft ball of positive stuff with electrons dotted through it, like raisins in a pudding.
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. 1904 plum-pudding atom: soft positive sphere with electron raisins dotted through. Continuous gentle rotate. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. Not photoreal food only.
plates.prompt_try2: Same plum-pudding model, wider hero turn. Continuous turn. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: a soft ball of positive stuff with electrons dotted through it, like raisins in a pudding.
plates.prompt: Same plum-pudding model. Electron raisins settle into the soft positive ball. Continuous settle. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit.
plates.prompt_try2: MCU raisins nesting in the soft sphere. Continuous nest. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.prompt: Same plum-pudding model. Lovely slow rotate — beautiful, calm. Continuous rotate. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit.
plates.prompt_try2: Same model, soft beauty light. Continuous gentle spin. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.prompt: Same plum-pudding model cracks and dissolves — lovely, and wrong. Continuous fail-dissolve. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. No Ken Burns only.
plates.prompt_try2: Same pudding collapses into crumbs and light. Continuous collapse. Silent. No Explorer.
